evals.prompt: Approve specs for planning, but they have not run a path-by-path flow judge yet.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval until approval-time spec judge evidence has zero blocking findings and readiness evidence is recorded.

evals.prompt: Review specs missing API shape, nullability, retries, logging, rollback, and human approval.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval, records concrete spec gaps, and routes repair instead of letting planners infer behavior.

evals.prompt: Repair readiness findings where Go, TypeScript, and protobuf null/omitted/enum semantics drift.
evals.expected_output: Updates canonical specs from the findings, relinks dependents, reruns readiness checks, and does not approve unless all gates and human approval pass.

evals.prompt: Review backend rebuild specs for GraphQL, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema entities, errors.yaml, service manifests, and database record mappings where old code has stale aliases and fallback synthesis.
evals.expected_output: Requires the clean-rebuild decision, source-contract inventory, generation map, generated package checks, strong boundary type policy, handwritten remainder, and compatibility/migration stance before approval.

evals.prompt: Plan implementation from a draft spec set with no approved readiness report.
evals.expected_output: Treats planning as a near miss and blocks with readiness review requirements instead of creating tickets.

evals.prompt: Approve specs that define behavior, contracts, and tests, but leave folder placement to implementation tickets.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval until specs define the general file/folder structure by domain/topic, ownership boundaries, shared/reusable module placement, generated artifact locations, and public entrypoint or operational asset locations, without requiring an exhaustive file list.

evals.prompt: Approve specs for auth and API keys where the readiness report has normal gates, but the specs omit signup/recovery flows, roles, database indexes, secret rotation, and unhappy-path tests.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval through the checklist index and relevant topic files, records relevant topic gaps with evidence, requires checklist_walk_gate and checklist_walk blocking_findings_count to reflect the gaps, and routes repair instead of planning.

evals.prompt: Approve specs that say to use best practices for a database schema and query layer with the latest ORM, but cite no official docs, release metadata, versions, or research.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval through current_dependency_research_gate until specs cite current primary docs/package or release metadata, chosen stable versions, database index/query/performance guidance, and rationale for any older pins or nonstandard choices.

evals.prompt: Approve specs for a SaaS app that mentions a React frontend, API backend, uploads, subscriptions, email notifications, search, analytics, admin support tools, and an AI summarizer, but the readiness report only walked auth, data, and deployment checklist topics.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval because the checklist walk skipped relevant high-level indexes and topic files. Requires frontend, backend, platform, product/domain, quality, and performance applicability evidence plus gaps or coverage for files/media, payments/entitlements, notifications, search/reporting/analytics, admin/support/governance, AI/ML/automation, runtime/platform, service topology, security/abuse, and performance/capacity before planning.

evals.prompt: Approve specs that define API endpoints, database tables, and tests, but do not list the application capabilities, frontend access paths, data lifecycle/PII retention, state transitions, or final states for exports, notifications, and background sync.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval through end_to_end_definition_gate and checklist_walk_gate until specs include a capability inventory and end-to-end definition chains covering actor/consumer, entrypoint/reachability, contracts, data touched, classification/PII retention/deletion/export/redaction, state transitions, side effects, permissions, errors, recovery, observability, acceptance, verification, owner, and final state or explicit N/A evidence.

evals.prompt: Approve specs that define UserDto, UserPayload, UserRecord, and UserSummary in different files but include no catalog, owners, or mappings showing why the shapes differ.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval through representation_reuse_gate until the specs provide a representation catalog with canonical sources, owners, classes, consumer lists, explicit mappings, permitted differences, and verification or scoped N/A evidence.

evals.prompt: Approve a spec set whose human approval was recorded before an API schema and mapping changed.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval until spec-manifest.yaml hashes every authoritative artifact, the content digest matches, provenance records the source revision, and fresh accountable approval evidence names that exact digest.

evals.prompt: Approve a representation catalog where User is listed but UserRead is only named by a mapping, mapping references are partial, and a nearby prose paragraph says N/A.
evals.expected_output: Blocks approval with exact catalog graph findings: every endpoint must be a registered shape, both shapes must reference each mapping, contract refs must resolve, and only scoped structured N/A evidence is accepted.

evals.prompt: Let an implementation agent decide whether to make an exported type, alter a public mapping default, or introduce a shared module because the spec is concise.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the decision unless decision-authority and reuse/module artifacts cite an approved D2/D3 decision. Allows only D0 mechanical and D1 private reversible choices under the declared autonomy budget.
